title: Career Roadmap: Data Analyst
summary: A Data Analyst collects, cleans, analyses, and interprets data to help organisations understand performance, identify trends, solve business problems, and make better decisions. The role combines statistics, SQL, spreadsheets, data visualisation, and communication.

blocks.text: Data Analyst

blocks.label: Recommended degree
blocks.text: B.Sc. in Data Science / Data Analytics

A Data Analyst collects, cleans, analyses, and interprets data to help organisations understand performance, identify trends, solve business problems, and make better decisions. The role combines statistics, SQL, spreadsheets, data visualisation, and communication.
flaex.ai
What does a Data Analyst do?
Retrieves data from databases, fixes data-quality problems, analyses trends, builds reports and dashboards, and translates findings into actionable recommendations.
Typical responsibilities
SQL queries, spreadsheet analysis, exploratory data analysis, KPI tracking, dashboard development, business reporting, and communicating insights to stakeholders.
Industries
IT services, banking, fintech, e-commerce, healthcare, education, logistics, telecommunications, consulting, and manufacturing.

rows.text: Mathematics is strongly recommended; statistics and computer science are useful
B.Sc. in Data Science, Data Analytics, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related discipline
Commonly 3 or 4 years, depending on the institution and programme structure
Statistics, probability, databases, programming, data visualisation, and business fundamentals
M.Sc. Data Science, Statistics, Business Analytics, Applied Mathematics, or an MBA in Business Analytics

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: A B.Sc. in Data Science is not the only route into this career. Employers may also consider candidates from statistics, mathematics, economics, commerce, and computer science who demonstrate relevant analytical skills.
The roadmap below is organised by academic year. Adapt the final year to your university's degree duration and curriculum.
Year 1
Statistics, spreadsheets, and programming

items.text: Learn descriptive statistics, probability, distributions, and basic inference.
Learn Excel or Google Sheets, including formulas, sorting, filtering, PivotTables, and charts.
Learn Python fundamentals, functions, data structures, and file handling.
Practise NumPy, pandas, and Matplotlib.
Learn basic SQL queries using SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, and GROUP BY.
Complete a small data-cleaning and visualisation project.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: take a raw dataset, clean it, calculate summary statistics, and explain its main patterns.
Year 2
SQL, analytics, and dashboards

items.text: Learn joins, subqueries, CTEs, window functions, and aggregate queries.
Study sampling, hypothesis testing, correlation, regression, and confidence intervals.
Learn Power BI or Tableau, including data modelling, calculated measures, and dashboard design.
Practise exploratory data analysis and business KPI definitions.
Build two projects using realistic business datasets.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: independently answer business questions using SQL and communicate results through a dashboard.
Year 3
Applied analytics and industry exposure

items.text: Learn advanced SQL, data validation, data storytelling, and analytical problem-solving.
Explore A/B testing, customer segmentation, cohort analysis, and forecasting basics.
Learn how data is collected, stored, transformed, and used in reporting pipelines.
Complete an internship, live project, or research assignment where possible.
Create a portfolio containing SQL queries, analysis notebooks, and interactive dashboards.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: deliver an end-to-end analysis with clear recommendations and reproducible calculations.
Final year / optional Year 4
Specialisation and job preparation

items.text: Complete a capstone project using a substantial dataset.
Strengthen SQL, statistics, Excel, Power BI or Tableau, and Python.
Practise business case studies, metric interpretation, and communicating insights.
Learn basic Git and data-quality testing.
Apply for Data Analyst, Business Intelligence Analyst, Reporting Analyst, and Product Analyst roles that match your skills.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: present a polished portfolio and explain the business impact and limitations of your analysis.

blocks.label: Priority order for employability
blocks.text: Excel → SQL → Power BI → statistics → Python. This gives you a practical analytics toolkit while you develop deeper technical skills.
Spreadsheets
Microsoft Excel for cleaning data, formulas, PivotTables, quick analysis, and reporting.
Databases and SQL
PostgreSQL or MySQL for querying structured datasets. Practise with realistic multi-table databases.
Business intelligence
Microsoft Power BI or Tableau for interactive dashboards, data models, measures, and reporting.
Analytics programming
Python, pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Jupyter Notebook for data cleaning, statistical analysis, automation, and visualisation.
Portfolio and collaboration
Git and GitHub for version control, documenting analytical work, and sharing reproducible projects.
You do not need to learn every BI tool. Become proficient in one dashboard platform, one SQL database, and Python for analysis before expanding your stack.
Aim for three to five projects that demonstrate analytical thinking—not just attractive charts. Every project should answer a specific question and explain what decision its findings support.
Project 1 — Sales performance dashboard
Beginner
Analyse revenue, profit, product categories, regional performance, and monthly trends. Identify the strongest and weakest segments.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: Excel, SQL, Power BI.
Project 2 — E-commerce customer analysis
Beginner–Intermediate
Analyse repeat purchases, average order value, customer cohorts, retention, and product performance. Suggest evidence-based actions to improve customer experience.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: SQL, Python, pandas, Power BI or Tableau.
Project 3 — Marketing funnel analysis
Intermediate
Examine visits, leads, sign-ups, and purchases. Calculate conversion rates, compare campaign performance, and investigate where users drop off.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: SQL, Excel, Power BI, statistics.
Project 4 — Employee attrition analysis
Intermediate
Explore relationships between attrition, tenure, department, workload, and compensation using an appropriate dataset. Clearly distinguish correlations from causes.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: Python, pandas, statistics, visualisation.
Project 5 — End-to-end business intelligence project
Job-ready focus
Load data from multiple tables, clean and validate it, write reusable SQL queries, build a dashboard, and prepare an executive summary with recommendations.

blocks.label: Tools
blocks.text: PostgreSQL, Python, Power BI, GitHub.

blocks.label: Portfolio standard
blocks.text: Include the business problem, dataset source, cleaning steps, SQL queries, KPI definitions, charts, findings, recommendations, and limitations. Use public or properly authorised datasets, and do not expose confidential personal or company data.

rows.text: Spreadsheet projects, campus research, data-cleaning assignments

blocks.text: Explore opportunities in IT services, consulting, fintech, retail, healthcare, logistics, SaaS, and analytics teams within larger companies.

When reviewing an internship, look for hands-on SQL, reporting, data validation, dashboard creation, and business problem-solving. Be cautious of roles that promise a job but mainly sell training or require payment for placement.

Transition to Data Science
Business Intelligence
Prioritise Excel, SQL, Power BI or Tableau, data modelling, DAX where relevant, KPI design, and executive reporting. Best if you enjoy dashboards and business performance.

blocks.label: AI-assisted analytics
blocks.text: Use AI tools to help draft SQL, explain code, and explore data, while independently validating the results.

blocks.label: Self-service BI
blocks.text: Enable teams to answer routine questions through governed dashboards and reusable data models.

blocks.label: Analytics engineering
blocks.text: Transform raw data into tested, documented, business-ready datasets.

blocks.label: Real-time analytics
blocks.text: Analyse streaming events and operational data for faster decisions.

blocks.label: Experimentation and causal analysis
blocks.text: Move beyond simple correlations to evaluate whether interventions actually cause measurable changes.

blocks.label: Data governance and privacy
blocks.text: Improve data quality, access controls, documentation, and responsible use of sensitive information.
AI can speed up analysis, but it does not replace statistical reasoning, data validation, business understanding, or accountability for conclusions.

A competitive entry-level candidate should ideally demonstrate:

items.text: Strong SQL, spreadsheet, and data-visualisation skills.
A practical understanding of statistics and data quality.
Three to five original projects with documented findings and recommendations.
At least one interactive dashboard and one Python-based analysis.
The ability to explain how the analysis supports a business decision.

blocks.text: Example resume headline
Aspiring Data Analyst | SQL, Excel, Power BI & Python | Statistical Analysis, Data Visualisation & Business Intelligence | Analytics Portfolio Projects
Final recommendation
For a B.Sc. Data Science / Analytics student, prioritise Excel → SQL → Power BI → statistics → Python, then build a portfolio around sales, customer behaviour, marketing, finance, or operations.

The key distinction between a beginner and a job-ready Data Analyst is the ability to take an unclear business question, obtain and validate the right data, analyse it correctly, and communicate a useful recommendation—not simply produce charts or complete online certificates.
